topPRs.title: compliance: spec improvements from fma
topPRs.author: 0xOneTony
topPRs.body:
Spec fixes from the bridge hook FMA review, on top of #971, grouped by failure mode.

**FM2: Completions publish more deposit gas than one L2 block can take**
- The published deposit gas count covers the whole L1 block in which a hook is set or removed.

**FM3: A withdrawal calls the hook or the bridge's escrow functions**
- `completeWithdrawalTransaction` reverts if the target is an Unsafe Target at the time of completion.

**FM9: The policy screens the wrong parties**
- The policy always receives two parties, sender then recipient, decoded only from messages the messengers sent.
- The module reads the L1 bridge and messenger addresses from the Portal's `SystemConfig` when deployed.
- New `parties()` view returns the same two addresses.

**FM10: A clearance outlives the check it was written for**
- Completion passes the policy the record's `clearedAt`.

**FM12 / FM17: A compromised policy / a wrong disable cutoff**
- `setPolicy`, `disable` and `enable` emit `PolicySet`, `Disabled` (with the cutoff) and `Enabled`.

**FM13: The module's balance stops covering what it holds**
- The bridge moves held tokens before the hook records the hold.

**FM15: Non-standard tokens break holds or completions**
- The module supports ETH, Native L1 Tokens and `OptimismMintableERC20` tokens.

**FM19: The hook stands between governance and L2**
- `depositTransaction` skips the hook for deposits sent by the ProxyAdmin owner, so governance actions on L2 never wait on screening. The overview's goals note the exception.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/823

topPRs.title: zk: align ZK dispute game specs with the implementation
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
Brings the ZK dispute game specs in line with the monorepo implementation: fixes outdated contract details (game type, `SuperRootProof` encoding, verifier, OPCM config and validation, game mechanics), adds the public interface reference, rewrites migration around `upgrade()`/`migrate()`, documents the SP1 program structure and proof completeness, and adds an honest actors page. The ZK Fault Proof VM page is renamed to ZK Proof System (with a redirect), and the dispute game interface, portal and OPCM migrator pages get matching fixes.

Closes ethereum-optimism/proofs-team#9. Commits are self-contained and can be reviewed one by one.

topPRs.title: interop: Address review findings on message expiry
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Stacked on ethereum-optimism/specs#960. This change fixes the findings from a review of the message expiry specs.

Correctness:
- A message to a chain whose portal the source chain's `ETHLockbox` does not authorize can expire after the `ETHLockbox` authorizes it. The text no longer says such a message can never expire.
- A caller that shares the `ETHLockbox` is paused with the source chain, so a pause revert of `relayUndeliveredMessage` is not recorded as a failed message.
- `ETHLockbox` authorization is permanent. A chain whose portal moves to another lockbox can still attest. The aME-001 mitigation no longer claims a shared custody of ETH.

Structure:
- The `EXPIRY_PERIOD >= EXPIRY_WINDOW` rule is now stated once, as aME-002. The contract cannot enforce it.
- Process and tooling text is removed. The dependency set condition is now assumption aME-004.
- The new iME-006 holds the emit-once and record-every-relay rules from the safety argument.
- iEL-005 moves to the `L1CrossDomainMessenger` spec as invariant i01-006, because that contract owns the nonce. iEL-004 now depends on it. The iSEB-004 dependencies are corrected.
- The L1 unsafe targets text links to the existing `relayMessage` spec.
- "Expiring Messages" moves under "Interfaces", so that it no longer nests "Relaying Messages".

There are also smaller wording fixes.

topPRs.title: agents: Add specification consistency reviewer
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Add a repository-local consistency reviewer for specification reviews. The reviewer checks for conflicting requirements, stale statements, incomplete exhaustive lists, and differences between prose and pseudocode. It traces related sections beyond the changed lines and requires evidence for each finding.

The reviewer treats explicit hard fork changes as expected behavior, not contradictions. It checks scope, activation conditions, and amendments before it reports a conflict. Each finding identifies both source locations and explains why the statements cannot both apply.

The agent uses `model: inherit` and inherits available tools. Its instructions limit it to review without edits and exclude style, implementation quality, and protocol design reviews.
